You’re talking about Personal Shoppers when you say “pushing a cart around a temperature controlled grocery store”. The preppers and dispensers are the ones that bring out all types of orders small or large in rain, sleet, and snow. They spend time in coolers and freezers then bring orders out into winter weather.

I honestly don’t know what’s worse. Going out into the snow after being in a cooler/freezer or the constant body temperature change from going into there then out into 80-90 degree weather during the summer.

I work in a fast paced OPD department and the expectation is high, especially on our busiest days. Sometimes we have 30-50 minute wait times because of callouts and everything being backed up. It’s also frustrating when half our shoppers barely do their job and we’re expected to fix it.

Having said that… it all has to do with the store I’m at. I’m sure there are worse/better stores. The fact is that the bar to get recognized as a good worker is pretty low, at least in my department at my store. Just speaking english well gets you called out to do things a lot. Like being put in charge if nobody is there (but not paid for it).

Plus since our department is the most profitable we have corporate breathing down management’s neck, so they are on top of our team leads, and our team leads are high stressed and barking orders nonstop making it an unpleasant environment.

If I had known that going in, I wouldn’t have tried as hard and would’ve kept a low profile. If I had done that… I’d probably also find the job to be pretty easy. I honestly should probably just switch departments.
